question: What is the major function of a cell wall?

options.text: It works as a storage for material
It provides shape and rigidity to the cell
It is responsible for cell division
It helps in synthesis of carbohydrate

solution:
The correct answer is __**It provides shape and rigidity to the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell walls **are a feature of almost all** prokaryotic cells**, as well as many **eukaryotic organisms.**
 
• In addition to providing structural support and maintaining the shape of the cell, The cell wall serves as a **protective barrier** against **physical** and** biological threats.**
 
• It also allows the cell to **withstand** the difference in **osmotic pressure** between the **cell's interior and its environment.**
 
• However, it is not primarily involved in functions such as storage of material, cell division, or the synthesis of carbohydrates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The structure of a typical cell, whether it is a **prokaryotic cell (such as bacteria)** or a **eukaryotic cell (like those found in plants and animals),** includes several key components:

 
• **Cell Membrane (Plasma Membrane):** It controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell.
 
• **Cytoplasm: **This is the jelly-like substance within the cell membrane, which contains all the organelles.
 
• **Nucleus:** In eukaryotic cells, this organelle contains the cell's DNA and controls the cell's growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• **Mitochondria: ** They generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER):** There are two types: rough ER, which has ribosomes on its surface, and smooth ER, which lacks ribosomes.
 
• **Golgi Apparatus:** This organelle is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins for secretion.
 
• **Lysosomes: **They digest excess or worn-out organelles, food particles, and engulfed viruses or bacteria.
 
• **Ribosomes:** They can be found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• **Vacuoles:** These are storage bubbles found in cells. 
 
• **Cell Wall (only in plant cells, fungi, and some protists and bacteria):** It provides and maintains the shape of these cells and serves as a protective barrier.
 
• **Chloroplasts (only in plant cells and some protists):** They are the site of photosynthesis, where light energy is converted into chemical energy.
